extracted.intended_audience: college instructors and students in composition / English prose anthologies
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and selection criteria for an anthology used in college composition classes: how to choose, arrange, and use prose selections to teach writing, discussion, and style. Also includes Project Gutenberg distribution/license requirements for the eBook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement by related groups representing phases of life
rubrics_metrics.description: The selections ... have been arranged under a scheme which the editors believe to be new. There are nine related groups. Each successive group represents a different phase of life, beginning with character and personality, and concluding with art and literature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize an anthology thematically so each group represents a coherent phase of life or related topic, enabling a body of ideas that includes major human interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer full, rich, complex matter to formal drills
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors believe heartily with Pater that 'the chief stimulus of good style is to possess a full, rich, complex matter to grapple with'. Instruction in writing too often neglects this sound doctrine and places an emphasis upon formal matters that seems disproportionate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose readings with substantive content that gives students something meaningful to express; avoid overemphasis on isolated formal exercises at the expense of content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat form and content together
rubrics_metrics.description: Form and content go together and one must not suffer at the expense of the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When teaching composition, integrate instruction in formal technique with engagement with substantive ideas rather than separating them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selections should arouse thought and provoke oral discussion
rubrics_metrics.description: They have therefore aimed to present a series of related selections that would arouse thought and provoke oral discussion in the class-room, as well as furnish suitable models of style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select texts that stimulate classroom discussion and critical thinking, not merely passive reading; use them as springboards for oral and written work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use pieces that require extended classroom treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases the pieces are too long to be adequately handled in one class hour. A live topic may well be discussed for several hours, until its various sides have been examined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer longer/denser selections that warrant multiple class periods to examine different facets and promote deeper engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide selections as models of style
rubrics_metrics.description: The selections ... would arouse thought and provoke oral discussion in the class-room, as well as furnish suitable models of style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include exemplary prose that students can study for tone, diction, sentence structure, and rhetorical strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a variety of forms and subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Variety in form and subject-matter is fully as important as richness of content. Teachers of composition everywhere are becoming distrustful of an arrangement which is frankly at variance with the actual practice of writing ... The editors have deliberately avoided ... choosing pieces of one type to the exclusion of all others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the anthology covers multiple discourse types (description, exposition, narration, argument) and diverse topics to reflect real writing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid confining students to a single form of discourse
rubrics_metrics.description: It is better to set the student to the task of composition without confining him too narrowly to one form of discourse.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design assignments and readings that allow practice across genres rather than strict compartmentalization into single-form drills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary readings with definite theme-subject suggestions
rubrics_metrics.description: Much attention has been given to the suggestions at the end of the volume ... This aim ... could best be attained by providing for each group of selections definite suggestions of theme-subjects to be derived by the student from supplementary readings closely related to that group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pair each thematic group with directed supplementary readings and concrete topic prompts so students can derive composition themes from related materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: End-of-volume suggestions must be practically serviceable and avoid duplication
rubrics_metrics.description: Much attention has been given to the suggestions at the end of the volume with the aim of making them practically serviceable and, at the same time, as free as possible from duplication of class work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose homework and exercise prompts that complement in-class activities rather than repeating them; make them usable and distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selections should stimulate instructor contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors have aimed ... to supply selections so rich and vital in content that instructors themselves will feel challenged to add to the class discussion from their own knowledge and experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose texts that invite teachers to bring in background, anecdotes, or expertise to enrich discussion and model engaged scholarship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include narrative examples with plot (short stories)
rubrics_metrics.description: And in order to meet their requirements even more adequately, the editors have included two short stories at the end, as examples of narration with a plot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure anthology contains example narratives that demonstrate plot structure and story-telling techniques for teaching narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use selections to awaken students to many questions at issue
rubrics_metrics.description: A live topic may well be discussed for several hours, until its various sides have been examined and students are awakened to the many questions at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor texts that present complexity and ambiguity to generate multi-sided inquiry and critical thinking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer selections that are 'too long' only when they deepen study
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases the pieces are too long to be adequately handled in one class hour. A live topic may well be discussed for several hours...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance length with pedagogical payoff: longer pieces are appropriate when they meaningfully support extended analysis or practice.
